brief: Zero Hedge reviews Morgan Stanley strategist Nick Savone's weekly "Global Reflections" note after the S&P 500 fell for a seventh straight session (worst week since Liberation Day) and the Nasdaq entered a bear market, down on the year less than seven weeks after being up 18.7%. Savone frames the question as whether this is still an AI unwind or a broader growth scare; Morgan Stanley's house view is firmly bullish (Wilson targets S&P 8,700), but Savone's own evidence is more mixed, and the author notes the note omits Nvidia's Jensen Huang resignation and an SEC probe. Nvidia beat and guided higher yet fell 22.7%, now at a record 50% discount to the S&P. Selling spread to a record staples-over-tech rotation, gold (down a third since January), and Asia (Taiwan -6.2%, Korea -5.2% Friday). Hedge fund leverage is near COVID lows without calming markets. Morgan Stanley's derivatives desk says stocks bottom once the 62bps of priced Fed hikes come out, mirroring 2018, but the bank's own economist still expects hikes in December and March. The bull case needs the Fed to stop and untested earnings estimates to hold.
